children: Braze

shares fell about 12% in premarket trading Wednesday despite the customer-engagement software company reporting better-than-expected fiscal second-quarter results and raising its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook.
The software platform
reported Q2 non-GAAP EPS of $0.19, beating the consensus estimate by $0.03. Revenue rose 26% Y/Y to $227.2M, exceeding expectations by $6.94M.
The company expects fiscal 2027 revenue of $910M to $913M (
) and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.64 to $0.65 ($0.64 consensus). The revenue outlook represents growth of roughly 23% at the midpoint. For the third quarter, Braze
expects revenue of $229M to $230M and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.13 to $0.14.
The outlook comes as Braze

pushes further into artificial intelligence, with management highlighting growing adoption of its BrazeAI products and the opportunity to win customers that are still using older marketing technology.
Braze

is guiding for continued revenue growth but weaker near-term profitability, which could weigh more on the stock than its Q2 earnings beat. For Q3 FY2027, the company expects revenue of $229M-$230M ($228.80M consensus) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.13-$0.14 ($0.14 consensus)

Q2 subscription revenue rose to $207.7M, up 20.9% Y/Y, while professional services and other revenue more than doubled to $19.6M. Gross margins weakened slightly in Q2 66.8%, while non-GAAP gross margin was 68.6%.
Among customers generating at least $500,000 in annual recurring revenue, retention was 112%. Braze
ended the quarter with 2,789 customers, up from 2,422 a year earlier, including 361 customers with at least $500,000 in ARR versus 282 a year ago.
Braze
is positioning its AI products to help marketers automate customer engagement, from selecting target audiences to determining what content to deliver and when.
The company said adoption of BrazeAI Operator, Agent Console and Decisioning Studio accelerated during the quarter, supporting customer expansion and product-led growth.
